_comment: English Grade 1 Learner's Book — per-book overrides.
Every entry here corrects this manuscript's own slips or sizes this manuscript's
own pictures. None of it is an engine fault, so none of it belongs in src/typeset/.
DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED — the handwriting-practice rows. The /e/ lesson's practice
block reads 'C C C C C' over 'e e e e e', which looks like a typo for 'E'. It is not:
the book's first practice block sets out C, I, a and A together, and later lessons use
'I I I I I' and 'Th th th...'. C and I are the curve and the line — the STROKES a child
traces — not the letter the lesson happens to be teaching. Leave them alone.
_comment_authors: The manuscript names its author twice: the title page has 'Author / Yvonne
Kasongo', and the bio page gives her surname-first as 'Kasongo, Yvonne is an
experienced Zambian educator...'. House style is one form per person, the fullest
one, so the cover and title-page byline carry 'Yvonne Kasongo'. The engine found
no byline of its own (the manuscript's title page is a picture, not text), so it

_comment_artSlots: PICTURE SLOTS. The author wrote her pictures as instructions in the text rather than
drawing them — "Picture of a snake", "We help the elderly (picture here)". Typeset as
ordinary paragraphs they read as if a Grade 1 child were meant to read them, and the
page each picture needs is nowhere to be seen.
So each one becomes an open picture slot: a framed gap of the height the picture will
need, carrying the author's own words for whoever draws it. The numbers are the same
ones the picture brief uses (output/Grade 1/ENGLISH GRADE 1 LB/…Picture Brief.pdf), so
PIC 12 in the proof and PIC 12 in the brief are the same picture.
Heights are a judgement from what each note has to show: 80mm for a whole scene (a
market, a school area, people doing several things), 62mm for a set of small spot
drawings, 48mm for a single object.
60 slots are listed here. 4 more picture notes are NOT slots because the author
already pasted a picture at that spot — PIC 1, 7, 11, 15;
those notes are stray lines to delete once the pasted picture is confirmed as the one
the note asks for.
Nine numbers are deliberately missing from the list. They were slots once, but a
look at the proof showed none of them is a missing picture:
PIC 5, 8, 9, 54   the author's picture is already pasted directly above (the family,
the umbrella, the four chores photos, the five song panels); the
'note' is the learner's instruction about it ('Look at the
picture. Name the people and their chores') and prints as text
PIC 25, 34, 72    the same: an activity instruction about the picture just before
it (the market, the /sh/ picture, the market people)
PIC 52, 74        a description of the picture just before it, so it is folded
into PIC 51's and PIC 73's note and deleted (see deleteExact)
The numbers are kept, not closed up, so the picture brief still lines up.
PIC 4, 33, 39, 42 and 71 carry a `note` for the same reason PIC 62 does: the author
wrote the picture's description on the lines after the note, and those lines printed
as learner text. Each description now lives in the note and the lines are deleted.
This whole block is scaffolding for the drawing stage. As each picture arrives, give
its entry an `art` path (in ENGLISH GRADE 1 LB-art/, named picNN-...) and the slot
prints the picture instead; the book is finished when every entry has its art.

_comment_editAll: AUTHOR SLIPS in the front matter, each settled by the manuscript itself or by plain
fact — nothing here is a judgement call:
AKNOWLEDGEMENT                       -> ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
Zambia Educational Publish House     -> ...Publishing House (the imprint page three
lines above spells it in full)
Lusaka, Zambi                        -> Lusaka, Zambia
Chisango Road                        -> Chishango Road (ZEPH is on Chishango Road)
Permanent Secretary –Adminitration   -> Permanent Secretary – Administration
ENTERPRENUARSHIP                     -> ENTREPRENEURSHIP (Unit 7; the book spells it
a third way at Unit 16 — one spelling, the
correct one, for both)
FARMIMG                              -> FARMING (Unit 13)
UNIT 5 TOURISM                       -> UNIT 5: TOURISM (every other unit heading in
the book puts a colon after the number)
UNIT:14 NATIONAL VALUES              -> UNIT 14: NATIONAL VALUES (same, with the
colon on the wrong side of the number)
How are you? Put picture             -> How are you? (the greeting exchange reads
'How are you?' / 'I am fine'; 'Put picture'
is the author's note to the illustrator, and
the picture it asks for is PIC 2 right below)
envelop                              -> envelope (the /e/ word list: egg, elephant,
envelope)
cI                                   -> cl (the consonant-blend list reads
'cI bl fl gl pl' — a capital I for a
lowercase l; every other blend in the line
is consonant + l. 'cI' occurs exactly once
in the manuscript, so the find is safe)
managing glasses                     -> magnifying glasses (the I-spy game: two
children looking through them, saying
'I spy green')
LESSSON                              -> LESSON (once, the /e/ lesson heading)
Sheepshop                            -> Sheep shop (the /sh/ word list, which the
author typed with no spaces at all)
The unit headings feed the contents page, so fixing the heading fixes both.
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT also has to be spelled right for the engine to see it as a section at
all: mis-spelled, it was not recognised as a heading and the whole acknowledgement ran
into the preface signature block above it.
_comment_deleteExact: PIC 62's picture note runs over THREE manuscript paragraphs. Only the first line
("pictures of a teacher standing") became the slot, so the other two printed below it
as if a Grade 1 learner were meant to read them. The slot's `note` now carries the
whole description — and its height goes 48mm -> 80mm, because it turns out to be a
whole classroom scene rather than the single figure the first line suggested. The two
run-on lines are deleted here. (Their 'flour' and 'clothe' are corrected to 'floor'
and 'cloth' inside the note; 'Sit on the floor' two lines further down the page settles
the first, and nothing is hanging on flour.)
The manuscript heads its imprint page "Author / Yvonne Kasongo" and then heads the
bio page "AUTHOR" as well, so the book opened with two AUTHOR sections one page apart.
The imprint page needs neither: the cover and the title page both carry the byline, and
the bio page is the real author section. Both lines go; the imprint keeps its address.
The rest are picture descriptions written as run-on lines after a picture note (PIC 4,
33, 39, 42, 52, 71, 74 — see _comment_artSlots). The description now lives in the
slot's `note`; 'short and shirt' is read as 'shorts and a shirt' there.
